### Executive Summary
A research study conducted by Omdia and sponsored by Object First reveals a significant operational gap in organizational ransomware defenses. While 93% of technology leaders agree that absolutely immutable backup storage is critical for ransomware protection, only 16% currently possess it.

This disconnect highlights a widespread vulnerability in enterprise data resilience, where the vast majority of organizations recognize the necessity of immutable data architecture but have yet to deploy it effectively.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause
The technical root cause of this exposure is the low implementation rate of immutable backup storage architecture across enterprise environments, leaving 84% of surveyed organizations without this safeguard.

Without immutable backup controls, backup storage remains susceptible to tampering, encryption, or deletion during a cyber incident. This severely impacts an organization's capability to safely restore systems and operational data following a ransomware outbreak.

### Mitigation & IOCs
Technology leaders and security teams should evaluate current data protection architectures and implement verified immutable backup storage solutions to ensure data integrity during a ransomware attack.
